question: When did the Government of India bring the gender sensitivities of the budgetary allocation in its statement for the first time?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2005-06.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Gender Budgeting exercise in India was formally introduced for the first time in the Union Budget of 2005-06, when a separate Gender Budget Statement (GBS) was included in the budget documents. (लैंगिक बजट — 2005-06)

 

• Gender Budgeting is a tool of applying gender mainstreaming in the budgetary process, meaning a gender-based assessment of budgets, incorporating a gender perspective at all levels of the budgetary process.

 

• The Ministry of Women and Child Development (MWCD) is the nodal ministry for the Gender Budgeting initiative in India and coordinates the preparation of the Gender Budget Statement every year.

 

• The Gender Budget Statement is divided into Part A (schemes with 100% provision for women) and Part B (schemes with at least 30% provision for women).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• India was among the early adopters of gender budgeting among developing nations, following countries like Australia (which pioneered it in the 1980s).

 

• Gender Budgeting Cells (GBCs) have since been set up in various central ministries and departments to institutionalise the process.

 

NOTE

 

• 2004-05 (Option 1): No formal Gender Budget Statement was presented in this year; the initiative began the following fiscal year.

 

• 2007-08 (Option 2): By this year, gender budgeting was already an established practice, not its point of introduction.

 

• 2006-07 (Option 3): This was the second year of the gender budgeting exercise, not its first.

question: Which of these measures of money supply is referred to as the aggregate monetary resources?
solution_text:
The correct answer is M3.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• M3, one of the four standard measures of money supply defined by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), is officially referred to as "Aggregate Monetary Resources" (AMR). (मुद्रा आपूर्ति — M3)

 

• M3 = M1 + Time deposits with the banking system, and M1 = Currency with the public + Demand deposits with banks + Other deposits with RBI.

 

• M3 is the broadest and most commonly used measure of money supply in India for monetary policy analysis, as it captures both the highly liquid components (M1) and the less liquid time deposits.

 

• It is also sometimes called "Broad Money".

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• M2 = M1 + Savings deposits with Post Office savings banks, and is more liquid than M3 but less commonly used than M1 or M3.

 

• M4 = M3 + All deposits with Post Office savings banks (excluding National Savings Certificates) and is the least liquid measure of money supply.

 

NOTE

 

• M4 (Option 1): This is the broadest measure including post office deposits, but it is not the one termed "aggregate monetary resources"; it is the least liquid measure.

 

• M1 (Option 2): Known as "Narrow Money", it is the most liquid measure, not the aggregate monetary resources.

 

• M2 (Option 3): This is an intermediate measure between M1 and M3, not designated as aggregate monetary resources.

question: _______ is/are an item for which both, GST and central excise duty are applicable in India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tobacco and tobacco products.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Tobacco and tobacco products (such as cigarettes) are unique in India in that they attract GST, GST Compensation Cess, AND Central Excise Duty simultaneously — the Central Government retained a residual excise duty on tobacco even after GST was rolled out, to protect its own revenue stream and to discourage consumption. (तंबाकू उत्पाद — GST तथा उत्पाद शुल्क दोनों)

 

• Under the Goods and Services Tax (GST) regime that came into effect on 1 July 2017, most indirect taxes including central excise duty were subsumed into GST.

 

• However, five commodities — petroleum crude, petrol, diesel, ATF (aviation turbine fuel), and natural gas — were kept entirely outside GST and continue to attract only central excise duty (by the Centre) and VAT (by the states), not GST.

 

• Alcohol for human consumption is also kept entirely outside GST; it is taxed only by state excise duty and state VAT, not by any central levy.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The dual levy on tobacco (GST + excise) is meant to keep the effective tax burden on tobacco products high, given their status as a demerit/sin good.

 

• GST Council has periodically discussed bringing petroleum products under GST but no consensus has been reached as of now.

 

NOTE

 

• Alcohol for human consumption (Option 1): Entirely outside the GST net; only state excise duty and VAT apply, not central excise or GST.

 

• Petroleum products (Option 3): Also kept outside GST; they attract only central excise duty and state VAT, not GST.

 

• All the agricultural commodities (Option 4): Most unprocessed agricultural produce is exempt from GST altogether and does not attract central excise duty either.

question: Who among the following was the Governor General of India when the Permanent Settlement was introduced in Bengal for revenue collection by the East India Company?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lord Cornwallis.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Permanent Settlement (Zamindari System) was introduced in Bengal and Bihar in 1793 by Lord Cornwallis, who was Governor-General of India from 1786 to 1793. (स्थायी बंदोबस्त — लॉर्ड कार्नवालिस)

 

• Under this system, Zamindars were recognised as the permanent, hereditary owners of land, in exchange for a fixed annual revenue payable to the Company, irrespective of the actual agricultural output.

 

• It was formulated with the advice of John Shore and James Grant, and was intended to create a loyal landed gentry supportive of British rule while ensuring a stable and predictable revenue stream.

 

• Lord Cornwallis is also known for the Cornwallis Code (1793), which established the separation of the judiciary from the executive and laid down civil service reforms.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Two other land revenue systems introduced later were the Ryotwari System (introduced by Thomas Munro and Alexander Read in Madras and Bombay presidencies) and the Mahalwari System (introduced in the Ganga Valley, North-West Provinces, and Punjab).

 

• The Permanent Settlement is widely criticised for impoverishing peasants and creating an exploitative intermediary class of zamindars.

 

NOTE

 

• Lord Wellesly (Option 2): Governor-General from 1798-1805, known for introducing the Subsidiary Alliance System.

 

• Lord Dalhousie (Option 3): Governor-General from 1848-1856, known for the Doctrine of Lapse.

 

• Lord Canning (Option 4): The last Governor-General and first Viceroy of India, in office during the Revolt of 1857.

question: The length of the playing surface for Table Tennis is ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2.74 m.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the rules laid down by the International Table Tennis Federation (ITTF), the playing surface (table top) for Table Tennis is 2.74 m (9 feet) long and 1.525 m (5 feet) wide. (टेबल टेनिस — 2.74 मीटर लंबाई)

 

• The table top must be positioned 76 cm (2 feet 6 inches) above the floor and must be made of any material yielding a uniform bounce of about 23 cm when a standard ball is dropped from a height of 30 cm.

 

• The table is divided into two equal courts by a vertical net, which is 15.25 cm (6 inches) high, running parallel to the end lines.

 

• Table Tennis was first included in the Olympic Games at Seoul in 1988, and its governing body ITTF was founded in 1926.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The standard table tennis ball has a diameter of 40 mm and weighs 2.7 grams.

 

• India's most celebrated Table Tennis players include Manika Batra, Sharath Kamal, and Sathiyan Gnanasekaran.

 

NOTE

 

• 3.74 m, 4.74 m and 5.74 m (Options 2, 3 and 4): These do not correspond to the ITTF-specified length of a table tennis table; they are incorrect distractor values.

question: Which state appointed Robin Uthappa as brand ambassador for the Brain Health Initiative in 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Karnataka.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Government of Karnataka appointed former Indian cricketer Robin Uthappa as the brand ambassador of the "Brain Health Initiative" in April 2022. (ब्रेन हेल्थ इनिशिएटिव — कर्नाटक)

 

• The initiative aims at improving awareness, diagnosis, and treatment of neurological disorders in the state, and was launched around World Brain Day 2022 (22 July).

 

• As part of the initiative, a Brain Health Clinic was also inaugurated in Karnataka to provide better neurological care.

 

• Robin Uthappa is a former Indian cricketer known for his role in India's victory in the 2007 ICC T20 World Cup.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Karnataka has also run other public health awareness campaigns in partnership with celebrities to widen their reach among the general population.

 

• World Brain Day is observed annually on 22 July, initiated by the World Federation of Neurology.

 

NOTE

 

• Tamil Nadu, West Bengal, and Odisha (Options 1, 2 and 3): None of these states appointed Robin Uthappa for the Brain Health Initiative; this was a Karnataka government initiative.

question: Who among the following long jumpers won the first ever silver medal for India in the long jump at commonwealth games 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Murali Sreeshankar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Murali Sreeshankar won India's first-ever silver medal in the men's long jump event at the 2022 Commonwealth Games held in Birmingham, with a jump of 8.08 m. (लंबी कूद — मुरली श्रीशंकर, रजत पदक)

 

• He is a prominent Indian long jumper from Kerala, trained by his father S. Murali, a former athlete himself.

 

• Sreeshankar had earlier also won gold at the 2022 National Games and set multiple national records in the long jump event.

 

• The gold medal in this event at CWG 2022 was won by Laquan Nairn of the Bahamas.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Murali Sreeshankar also competed in the 2023 World Athletics Championships, where he won a silver medal, becoming the first Indian male to win a medal in long jump at the World Championships.

 

• India's overall medal tally at the 2022 Commonwealth Games (Birmingham) was 61 medals (22 gold, 16 silver, 23 bronze).

 

NOTE

 

• Niraj Upadhyay (Option 1): Not associated with winning a silver medal in long jump at CWG 2022.

 

• Saurav Ghoshal (Option 2): An Indian professional squash player, not a long jumper; he won a bronze medal in squash at CWG 2022.

 

• Prashnata Sahoo (Option 4): Not associated with the long jump event at CWG 2022.

question: Which of the following universities was founded by Pala rulers?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vikramasila.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Vikramasila University was founded by Dharmapala, the second ruler of the Pala dynasty, in the late 8th century CE, in present-day Bhagalpur district, Bihar. (विक्रमशिला विश्वविद्यालय — पाल वंश)

 

• It became one of the two most important centres of Buddhist learning in India (along with Nalanda), specialising particularly in Tantric Buddhism, logic, and grammar.

 

• The famous Tibetan scholar Atisha Dipankara studied and later served as a senior teacher/abbot at Vikramasila before travelling to Tibet to spread Buddhism.

 

• The Pala dynasty (8th-12th century CE) ruled over Bengal and Bihar and were great patrons of Buddhism and Buddhist learning.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Both Vikramasila and Nalanda universities were destroyed by the forces of Bakhtiyar Khilji in the late 12th/early 13th century CE.

 

• The Palas also founded Odantapuri University in Bihar, another important seat of Buddhist learning.

 

NOTE

 

• Nalanda (Option 2): Traditionally credited to the Gupta ruler Kumaragupta I in the 5th century CE, though it received later patronage from the Palas.

 

• Valabhi (Option 3): A centre of Buddhist learning in Gujarat, patronised by the Maitraka dynasty, not the Palas.

 

• Taxila (Option 4): One of the oldest centres of learning in ancient India (in present-day Pakistan), pre-dating the Pala period by many centuries, associated with the Mauryan and earlier periods.

question: Gaan-Ngai is a five-day festival primarily celebrated in which part of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is North-Eastern.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Gaan-Ngai is a major five-day post-harvest festival celebrated by the Zeliangrong Naga tribe (Zeme, Liangmai, and Rongmei communities) primarily in Manipur, Nagaland and Assam, in North-Eastern India. (गान-नगाई महोत्सव — पूर्वोत्तर भारत)

 

• It is celebrated in the Naga month of Gaan (roughly corresponding to November-December) to mark the end of the harvest season and to seek blessings for prosperity in the coming year.

 

• The festival involves traditional dances, feasting, community bonding activities, and rituals invoking blessings from ancestors and deities.

 

• The Zeliangrong people are one of the major Naga ethnic groups spread across the North-Eastern states of Manipur, Nagaland and Assam.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other important festivals of the North-East include the Hornbill Festival (Nagaland), Bihu (Assam), and Losar (Sikkim/Arunachal Pradesh).

 

• Manipur is also known for other traditional festivals such as Lai Haraoba and Yaoshang.

 

NOTE

 

• Northern, Western, and Southern (Options 1, 3 and 4): Gaan-Ngai is not a traditional festival of these regions; it is specific to the Zeliangrong Naga communities of North-East India.

question: What is the aim of fundamental rights mentioned in the Indian Constitution?
solution_text:
The correct answer is To establish political democracy.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Fundamental Rights, enshrined in Part III (Articles 12-35) of the Indian Constitution, are aimed at establishing political democracy by guaranteeing individual liberty, equality, and protection against arbitrary state action. (मौलिक अधिकार — राजनीतिक लोकतंत्र)

 

• In contrast, the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP), given in Part IV (Articles 36-51), aim at establishing social and economic democracy (i.e., a welfare state and economic justice) by directing the state to work towards the well-being of the people.

 

• Fundamental Rights are justiciable (enforceable by courts under Article 32), whereas the DPSPs are non-justiciable but fundamental in the governance of the country.

 

• Dr. B.R. Ambedkar described Fundamental Rights and DPSP as complementary, together forming the conscience of the Constitution.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Fundamental Rights were inspired largely by the Bill of Rights of the United States Constitution.

 

• The Fundamental Rights currently include six categories: Right to Equality, Right to Freedom, Right against Exploitation, Right to Freedom of Religion, Cultural and Educational Rights, and Right to Constitutional Remedies (the Right to Property was removed as a Fundamental Right by the 44th Amendment, 1978).

 

NOTE

 

• To establish a welfare state (Option 1): This is the aim of the Directive Principles of State Policy, not the Fundamental Rights.

 

• To have an absolute independence (Option 2): Fundamental Rights are not absolute; they are subject to reasonable restrictions imposed by the state.

 

• To promote economic justice (Option 3): This is also primarily the objective of the Directive Principles of State Policy, aimed at establishing economic democracy.

question: What is the type of soil composed of silt and dust?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Loess.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Loess is a type of wind-deposited (aeolian) sediment, primarily composed of fine silt and dust particles, that has accumulated over long geological periods. (लोयस मृदा — सिल्ट और धूल)

 

• It is typically yellowish-buff in colour, highly fertile, and porous, making it agriculturally productive when properly managed.

 

• Major loess deposits are found in the Loess Plateau of China (along the Yellow River/Huang He), parts of the Mississippi and Missouri river valleys in the USA, and parts of Central Asia and Europe.

 

• Loess soils, being loosely compacted, are also prone to erosion and can be a source of significant sediment load in rivers flowing through such regions.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Yellow River (Huang He) in China derives its yellow colour and name from the vast quantities of loess silt it carries from the Loess Plateau.

 

• Loess is different from alluvial soil in that it is deposited by wind rather than by flowing water.

 

NOTE

 

• Loam (Option 1): A soil type composed of a balanced mixture of sand, silt, and clay, considered ideal for agriculture, but not specifically defined as silt-and-dust composed wind-blown soil.

 

• Marl (Option 2): A calcium carbonate-rich (limy) mud or mudstone containing clay and silt, formed typically in lake or marine environments, not primarily wind-deposited silt/dust.

 

• Podsol (Option 4): An acidic, nutrient-poor soil typically found in cool, moist, coniferous forest regions, characterised by leached upper layers, unrelated to wind-blown silt and dust.

question: Which of the following is NOT a fundamental duty mentioned in the Indian Constitution?
option_3: To develop the spirit of inquiry
option_4: To develop the spirit of harmony
solution_text:
The correct answer is To bring reform.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Fundamental Duties, listed under Article 51A in Part IV-A of the Indian Constitution (added by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976 on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee), do not list "to bring reform" as a standalone duty. (मौलिक कर्तव्य — अनुच्छेद 51A)

 

• Article 51A(h) obliges every citizen "to develop the scientific temper, humanism and the spirit of inquiry and reform" — here, "reform" appears only as part of this composite phrase ("spirit of inquiry and reform"), not as an independent, standalone duty of "bringing reform".

 

• Article 51A(e) obliges every citizen "to promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood amongst all the people of India", which corresponds to "developing the spirit of harmony".

 

• There are currently 11 Fundamental Duties in total, the 11th one (relating to a parent/guardian's duty to provide education) having been added later by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Fundamental Duties are not legally enforceable by courts, unlike Fundamental Rights, but they serve as a constant reminder to citizens of their obligations towards the nation.

 

• Fundamental Duties were inspired by the Constitution of the erstwhile USSR (Soviet Union).

 

NOTE

 

• To develop humanism (Option 2): Directly drawn from Article 51A(h) — "to develop the scientific temper, humanism and the spirit of inquiry and reform".

 

• To develop the spirit of inquiry (Option 3): Also directly drawn from Article 51A(h).

 

• To develop the spirit of harmony (Option 4): Drawn from Article 51A(e) — "to promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood".

question: Which is an inherited blood disorder that affects the hemoglobin gene and results in ineffective erythropoiesis?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Thalassemia.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Thalassemia is an inherited (genetic) blood disorder caused by mutations in the genes responsible for producing hemoglobin, leading to reduced or abnormal hemoglobin production and ineffective erythropoiesis (defective red blood cell production in the bone marrow). (थैलेसीमिया — वंशानुगत रक्त विकार)

 

• It results in varying degrees of anemia, with severity depending on the type — Thalassemia Major (Cooley's anemia), Thalassemia Intermedia, and Thalassemia Minor (trait).

 

• It is broadly classified into Alpha-thalassemia and Beta-thalassemia, based on which globin chain (alpha or beta) of hemoglobin is affected.

 

• Patients with severe thalassemia typically require regular blood transfusions and iron chelation therapy to manage the disease.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• World Thalassemia Day is observed annually on 8 May to raise awareness about the disease.

 

• Thalassemia is particularly prevalent in populations from the Mediterranean region, Middle East, South Asia, and Southeast Asia (the so-called "thalassemia belt").

 

NOTE

 

• Somatostatinoma (Option 1): A rare neuroendocrine tumour of the pancreas or duodenum that secretes excess somatostatin; unrelated to hemoglobin or erythropoiesis.

 

• Venous Thromboembolism (Option 3): A condition involving blood clot formation in veins (as in deep vein thrombosis or pulmonary embolism); not a hemoglobin-gene disorder.

 

• Polycythemia vera (Option 4): A myeloproliferative disorder causing the bone marrow to produce too many red blood cells; it is an overproduction disorder, the opposite of ineffective erythropoiesis, and not primarily a hemoglobin-gene disorder.

question: Padayani is a folk dance from which state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kerala.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Padayani (also spelt Padeni) is a traditional ritualistic folk art form and dance performed in the temples of central Travancore region of Kerala, particularly associated with Bhadrakali temples. (पड़यानी नृत्य — केरल)

 

• It involves performers wearing large, elaborately painted face masks (Kolams) made from arecanut leaf sheaths, coconut fronds, and natural dyes, depicting deities, demons, animals, and ancestral spirits.

 

• The dance is performed to the accompaniment of traditional percussion instruments like the thappu and folk songs, typically as part of temple festivals following the harvest season.

 

• It is believed to have originated as a ritual performed to please Goddess Bhadrakali after her fierce battle with the demon Darika.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other important folk/ritual dance forms of Kerala include Theyyam, Mudiyettu, and Thira.

 

• Kerala's classical dance forms include Kathakali and Mohiniyattam.

 

NOTE

 

• Karnataka (Option 2): Known for folk forms like Yakshagana and Dollu Kunitha, not Padayani.

 

• Andhra Pradesh (Option 3): Known for folk forms like Kuchipudi (classical) and Burrakatha, not Padayani.

 

• Tamil Nadu (Option 4): Known for folk forms like Karagattam and Kummi, not Padayani.

question: Under which Ministry does the Indian Antarctic Act, 2022 aim at having India's own national measures for protecting the Antarctic environment along with the dependent and associated ecosystems and proposes to set up Indian Antarctic Authority (IAA)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ministry of Earth Sciences.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Indian Antarctic Act, 2022 was enacted to give India its own national legal framework for protecting the Antarctic environment and its dependent ecosystems, and it functions under the Ministry of Earth Sciences (MoES). (भारतीय अंटार्कटिक अधिनियम — पृथ्वी विज्ञान मंत्रालय)

 

• The Act provides for the establishment of a Committee on Antarctic Governance and Environmental Protection, referred to in earlier drafts as the Indian Antarctic Authority (IAA), chaired by the Secretary, Ministry of Earth Sciences, to regulate Indian activities in Antarctica.

 

• India's Antarctic research programme, including its research stations Maitri and Bharati, is coordinated by the National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR), Goa, which functions under the Ministry of Earth Sciences.

 

• The Act gives effect to India's obligations under the Antarctic Treaty (1959), the Protocol on Environmental Protection to the Antarctic Treaty (Madrid Protocol, 1991), and the Convention on the Conservation of Antarctic Marine Living Resources (CCAMLR).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's first Antarctic research station, Dakshin Gangotri, was established in 1983 (now decommissioned); currently active stations are Maitri (1989) and Bharati (2012).

 

• India acceded to the Antarctic Treaty in 1983 and became a Consultative Party in the same year.

 

NOTE

 

• Ministry of Power (Option 1): Deals with the generation, transmission, and distribution of electric power in India; unrelated to Antarctic governance.

 

• Ministry of Textiles (Option 3): Deals with the textile and handloom sector; unrelated to Antarctic governance.

 

• Ministry of Science and Technology (Option 4): Oversees scientific research bodies like DST and DBT, but India's Antarctic programme falls specifically under the Ministry of Earth Sciences, not this ministry.

question: Ustad Bismillah Khan is associated with which of the following instruments?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shehnai.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ustad Bismillah Khan (1916-2006) was the legendary Indian classical musician credited with bringing the Shehnai, traditionally a folk and ceremonial wind instrument, to the concert stage as a serious classical instrument. (शहनाई — उस्ताद बिस्मिल्लाह खान)

 

• He famously performed the Shehnai from the ramparts of the Red Fort on the eve of India's independence on 15 August 1947, and again on 26 January 1950 to mark the first Republic Day.

 

• He was awarded the Bharat Ratna, India's highest civilian award, in 2001, becoming only the third classical musician to receive it (after M.S. Subbulakshmi and Pandit Ravi Shankar).

 

• He also received the Padma Shri (1961), Padma Bhushan (1968), and Padma Vibhushan (1980) during his illustrious career.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bismillah Khan was born in Dumraon, Bihar, and spent most of his life associated with the city of Varanasi (Banaras), particularly the Vishwanath Temple.

 

• Other renowned instrumentalists include Pandit Ravi Shankar (Sitar), Ustad Zakir Hussain (Tabla), and Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia (Flute).

 

NOTE

 

• Veena (Option 2): Associated with artists like Chitti Babu and S. Balachander, not Bismillah Khan.

 

• Flute (Option 3): Associated with artists like Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia, not Bismillah Khan.

 

• Violin (Option 4): Associated with artists like Dr. L. Subramaniam and T.N. Krishnan, not Bismillah Khan.

question: Sociologist Jan Breman described the change in the nature of the relationship between landlords, belonging to the dominant class, and agricultural workers, belonging to the low caste, as a shift from ____________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is patronage to exploitation.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Dutch sociologist Jan Breman, in his study of agrarian relations in south Gujarat (notably documented in his book "Patronage and Exploitation: Changing Agrarian Relations in South Gujarat, India"), described how the traditional relationship between dominant-caste landlords and low-caste agricultural (bonded) labourers shifted from patronage to exploitation. (जन ब्रेमन — संरक्षण से शोषण तक)

 

• In the earlier, more "patronage"-based system, landlords provided a degree of paternalistic security and social protection to their attached (often Halpati) labourers in exchange for their loyalty and bonded labour.

 

• With the commercialisation of agriculture and increasing capitalist relations of production, this personalised patron-client bond broke down, and labour relations became more purely market-based and exploitative, stripped of earlier reciprocal social obligations.

 

• This work is frequently cited in Indian sociology (e.g. NCERT "Indian Society") as a key study on the transformation of rural agrarian labour relations under capitalism.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Jan Breman is also well known for his extensive work on informal labour, migration, and footloose labour in India, including studies of the Halpati community of south Gujarat.

 

• His other notable works include "Footloose Labour: Working in India's Informal Economy".

 

NOTE

 

• Tenant to tiller (Option 1): This phrase relates to land reform/tenancy reform debates ("land to the tiller"), not to Breman's specific patronage-exploitation framework.

 

• Exploitation to patronage (Option 3): This reverses the actual direction of the change Breman documented; the shift was from patronage towards exploitation, not the other way round.

 

• Bonded labour to free labour (Option 4): While related to changing agrarian labour, this is not the specific terminology or framework Breman used to characterise the change in the landlord-labourer relationship.

question: Who first introduced the idea of a relationship between molecular geometry and the number of valence electrons in the 1940s?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sidgwick and Powell.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In 1940, British chemists Nevil Sidgwick and Herbert Powell first proposed the idea relating the geometry (shape) of molecules to the number of valence shell electron pairs around the central atom — the foundational concept behind what later became the VSEPR (Valence Shell Electron Pair Repulsion) theory. (संयोजकता कोश इलेक्ट्रॉन युग्म प्रतिकर्षण सिद्धांत — सिजविक और पॉवेल)

 

• Their original idea was later significantly extended and developed into the modern, fully-formulated VSEPR theory by Ronald Gillespie and Ronald Nyholm in 1957.

 

• The theory states that electron pairs (both bonding and lone pairs) around a central atom arrange themselves in space so as to minimise electrostatic repulsion between them, thereby determining the molecular geometry.

 

• VSEPR theory successfully explains and predicts shapes such as linear, trigonal planar, tetrahedral, trigonal bipyramidal, and octahedral geometries of molecules.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The theory is sometimes also referred to as the "Gillespie-Nyholm theory" in recognition of the scientists who fully developed it into its modern, widely-taught form.

 

• Other bonding theories used alongside VSEPR to explain molecular structure include Valence Bond Theory and Molecular Orbital Theory.

 

NOTE

 

• Bent and Nyholm (Option 1): Henry Bent is known for Bent's rule relating hybridisation to electronegativity, not the original 1940s proposal; Nyholm co-developed the later full VSEPR theory with Gillespie, not with Bent.

 

• Hendricus and Nicol (Option 2): Not associated with the historical development of VSEPR theory.

 

• Heitler and Gillespie (Option 4): Walter Heitler (with Fritz London) is known for pioneering Valence Bond Theory, an unrelated bonding concept; Gillespie later extended VSEPR with Nyholm, not with Heitler, and not in the 1940s.

question: According to the Ministry of Power, Government of India, which is the largest energy source of India? (as of March 2023)
solution_text:
The correct answer is Coal.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per data from the Ministry of Power, Government of India and the Central Electricity Authority (CEA), Coal remained India's single largest source of energy/electricity generation as of March 2023, accounting for roughly half of the country's total installed power generation capacity and an even larger share of actual electricity generated. (कोयला — भारत का सबसे बड़ा ऊर्जा स्रोत)

 

• India possesses the fourth/fifth-largest coal reserves in the world, and thermal (largely coal-based) power plants continue to form the backbone of India's base-load electricity supply.

 

• While India has been rapidly expanding its renewable energy capacity (solar, wind, etc.), coal-based thermal power still generates a much larger share of actual electricity units due to its ability to provide reliable, round-the-clock baseload power.

 

• India has committed under its international climate pledges to increase the share of non-fossil fuel-based energy capacity, but coal is expected to remain a dominant source in the near term.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's largest coal-producing states include Jharkhand, Odisha, Chhattisgarh, and Madhya Pradesh.

 

• Coal India Limited (CIL) is the world's largest coal-mining company by output, headquartered in Kolkata.

 

NOTE

 

• Hydro power (Option 1): An important renewable source but contributes a much smaller share of India's total installed capacity/generation compared to coal.

 

• Tidal energy (Option 2): A negligible and largely untapped source of energy in India's current energy mix.

 

• Solar energy (Option 4): A rapidly growing renewable source, but as of March 2023 its installed capacity and generation share were still well below that of coal.

question: Jayalakshmi Eshwar won the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award 2021 for her contribution to which Indian classical dance form?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bharatanatyam.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Jayalakshmi Eshwar, a renowned Chennai-based dancer and choreographer, was conferred the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for 2021 for her contribution to Bharatanatyam, one of the oldest classical dance forms of India. (भरतनाट्यम — जयलक्ष्मी ईश्वर)

 

• The Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (also called the Akademi Puraskar) is the highest Indian recognition given to practising artists in the fields of music, dance, and drama, conferred by the Sangeet Natak Akademi, India's National Academy for Music, Dance and Drama, under the Ministry of Culture.

 

• Bharatanatyam is believed to have originated in Tamil Nadu, traditionally performed in Hindu temples, and is characterised by fixed upper torso, bent legs, intricate footwork, and an expressive vocabulary of gestures (mudras).

 

• The award for the year 2021 was among a batch of awards announced later, honouring artistes for the years 2019, 2020, and 2021 together, due to delays caused by the COVID-19 pandemic.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Sangeet Natak Akademi was established in 1952 and is the oldest of the National Akademis of arts set up by the Government of India.

 

• Other prominent Bharatanatyam exponents who have received this award over the years include Padma Subrahmanyam and Chitra Visweswaran.

 

NOTE

 

• Kathakali (Option 2): A classical dance-drama form of Kerala, not the form for which Jayalakshmi Eshwar was honoured.

 

• Kathak (Option 3): A classical dance form primarily of North India, not associated with this award to Jayalakshmi Eshwar.

 

• Odissi (Option 4): A classical dance form of Odisha, not associated with this award to Jayalakshmi Eshwar.

question: Which state in India had the lowest sex ratio according to the 2011 census?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Haryana.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the 2011 Census of India, Haryana recorded the lowest sex ratio among all Indian states, at 879 females per 1000 males. (लिंगानुपात — हरियाणा सबसे कम)

 

• The national average sex ratio as per the 2011 Census was 943 females per 1000 males.

 

• Among Union Territories, Daman and Diu recorded the lowest sex ratio in 2011.

 

• Kerala had the highest sex ratio among Indian states in the 2011 Census, at 1084 females per 1000 males.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Beti Bachao Beti Padhao scheme was launched by the Government of India in 2015 partly in response to the declining child sex ratio, with Haryana's Panipat district chosen as the launch site.

 

• The child sex ratio (0-6 years) is tracked separately and has also historically been a concern in states like Haryana and Punjab.

 

NOTE

 

• Punjab (Option 1): Also had a relatively low sex ratio (895) in the 2011 Census, but not the lowest among states.

 

• Rajasthan (Option 2): Had a sex ratio of 928 in the 2011 Census, higher than Haryana's.

 

• Bihar (Option 3): Had a sex ratio of 918 in the 2011 Census, higher than Haryana's.

question: In India, the financial year runs from______ to _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is April 1, March 31.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In India, the financial year (fiscal year), used for government budgeting, taxation, and most corporate accounting, runs from 1 April of one calendar year to 31 March of the following calendar year. (वित्तीय वर्ष — 1 अप्रैल से 31 मार्च)

 

• This practice was adopted from the British colonial-era administrative calendar and has continued in independent India for consistency in accounting, taxation, and budget-making.

 

• The Union Budget of India is presented by the Finance Minister, and since 2017, it is presented on 1 February each year, applicable to the financial year starting the following 1 April.

 

• The NK Singh Committee (2016) examined the possibility of shifting India's fiscal year to align with the calendar year (January-December) but the government decided to retain the existing April-March cycle.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Many other countries, such as the USA (federal fiscal year: 1 October-30 September) and some others follow different fiscal year cycles; a number of countries, however, do follow the calendar year (January-December) as their fiscal year.

 

• The Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India audits government accounts prepared as per this April-March financial year.

 

NOTE

 

• February 1, January 31 (Option 2): Not India's financial year cycle; 1 February is only the date on which the Union Budget is presented.

 

• July 1, June 31 (Option 3): Not India's financial year cycle (and note, 31 June does not even exist as a calendar date).

 

• January 1, December 31 (Option 4): This is the standard calendar year, not India's official financial year.

question: The dimensions of force are:
solution_text:
The correct answer is [M L T⁻²].

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Force (F) is defined by Newton's Second Law as F = mass × acceleration = m × a. (बल का विमीय सूत्र — [M L T⁻²])

 

• Mass (m) has the dimension [M], and acceleration (a) (rate of change of velocity) has the dimension [L T⁻²] (length per time squared).

 

• Multiplying these gives the dimensional formula of force: [M] × [L T⁻²] = [M L T⁻²].

 

• The SI unit of force is the Newton (N), where 1 N = 1 kg·m/s², consistent with this dimensional formula.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The dimensional formula of pressure (Force/Area) is [M L⁻¹ T⁻²], and of energy/work (Force × Distance) is [M L² T⁻²].

 

• Dimensional analysis is a useful tool to check the correctness of physical equations (principle of homogeneity of dimensions) and to derive relationships between physical quantities.

 

NOTE

 

• [M⁰ L³ T⁰] (Option 1): This represents the dimensional formula of volume, not force.

 

• [M L⁻³ T⁰] (Option 2): This represents the dimensional formula of density, not force.

 

• [M⁰ L T⁻¹] (Option 3): This represents the dimensional formula of velocity/speed, not force.

question: Who among the following was one of the founders of the Indian Association, established in 1876?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Surendranath Banerjee.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Indian Association was founded in Calcutta in 1876 by Surendranath Banerjee and Anand Mohan Bose, and became one of the earliest and most influential pre-Congress political organisations in India. (इंडियन एसोसिएशन — सुरेंद्रनाथ बनर्जी)

 

• It was formed with the objective of creating a strong body of public opinion in the country and uniting Indians on a common political platform, and it played an important role in agitations such as the one against the Ilbert Bill (1883) and the reduction of the age limit for the Indian Civil Service (ICS) examination.

 

• The Indian Association later merged with the Indian National Congress after the latter's formation in 1885.

 

• Surendranath Banerjee was popularly known as "Rashtraguru" and "Surrender Not Banerjee" (a pun on his name, referencing his fighting spirit), and he twice served as President of the Indian National Congress (1895 and 1902).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Surendranath Banerjee also founded the Ripon College (later Surendranath College) in Calcutta and edited the newspaper "The Bengalee".

 

• Other important pre-Congress associations included the Poona Sarvajanik Sabha (1870) and the Bombay Presidency Association (1885).

 

NOTE

 

• Dadabhai Naoroji (Option 1): A prominent early nationalist leader and author of the "Drain of Wealth" theory, associated with the East India Association and later the Indian National Congress, but not a founder of the Indian Association.

 

• Mahadev Govind Ranade (Option 3): A founder of the Poona Sarvajanik Sabha and the Indian National Social Conference, not the Indian Association.

 

• Sisir Kumar Ghosh (Option 4): A journalist and founder of the newspaper "Amrita Bazar Patrika", not a founder of the Indian Association.

question: What is the phenomenon called when rain fails to occur for one or more weeks during the south-west monsoon period?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Break in the monsoon.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A "Break in the Monsoon" refers to a period during the south-west monsoon season (June-September) when rainfall ceases or is significantly reduced for one or more weeks over large parts of the country, even though the monsoon season has not yet withdrawn. (मानसून का विराम — वर्षा रुकना)

 

• Such breaks are typically caused by a northward shift of the monsoon trough (ITCZ) towards the Himalayan foothills, which temporarily reduces rainfall over the plains while increasing it in the sub-Himalayan region.

 

• Breaks in the monsoon are more common during July and August, and prolonged breaks can lead to agricultural drought-like conditions even in an otherwise normal monsoon year.

 

• This phenomenon is distinct from the onset and withdrawal phases of the monsoon, which mark its beginning and end respectively.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The south-west monsoon typically sets in over Kerala around 1 June and withdraws from Rajasthan by around mid-September, as per the India Meteorological Department (IMD) normal dates.

 

• Monsoon depressions, low-pressure systems that form over the Bay of Bengal, are actually associated with increased rainfall, not a break in rainfall.

 

NOTE

 

• Withdrawal of the monsoon (Option 1): Refers to the retreat of the monsoon system at the end of the rainy season (around September-October), not a temporary rainless spell within the season.

 

• El Nino (Option 3): A large-scale oceanic-atmospheric phenomenon involving the warming of central and eastern Pacific Ocean waters, which can weaken the Indian monsoon overall, but is not itself the term for a temporary within-season rainless spell.

 

• Monsoon depression (Option 4): A low-pressure weather system that actually brings heavy rainfall to the regions it affects, the opposite of a rainless break.
